caption:
Sends to a friend matter more than comments. Mosseri said it on October 23, 2026.

This quietly invalidates most of what gets sold as "engagement strategy". Comment pods, "tag 3 friends", bait questions in the caption, arguing in your own replies to push the count up — all of it optimises the weaker signal.

Here's why sends win, and it isn't arbitrary. A comment is a public performance; people leave them to be seen leaving them. A send is private. Nobody is watching. The only reason to DM your post to someone is that you genuinely believe it's worth that person's time — and you're putting your own judgement on the line by sending it.

That's a much harder thing to fake, which is exactly why the algorithm trusts it.

The practical shift is small and total: stop asking "what would make someone reply to this" and start asking "who would someone send this to, and why". Those produce completely different posts.

One of them grows an account. The other grows a comment count.
